plan.summary: This 4-week block starts the 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one focused S&C session each week to fit around higher sparring and skill work. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the main squat pattern, and the main training starts in Week 2. The emphasis is simple, beginner-friendly full-body strength and power with controlled volume so you build force without carrying extra fatigue into boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general full-body strength and basic explosive qualities with simple lifts that recover well alongside boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main lifts and throws steadily while keeping total volume low enough for sparring and skill work.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift more of the work toward crisp power and speed expression while maintaining the strength you built.

exercises.name: 1a. Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height that lets you land softly and stable. Reset between reps and keep each jump fast and clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no safe box setup is available. Jump for height and stick the landing.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want an even simpler option. Start from a controlled dip and drive up fast.

exercises.name: 1b. Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.notes: Use a non-bouncing or low-bounce ball if throwing to a wall. Drive the ball hard from the chest with full intent and reset each rep.

substitutionOptions.name: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if chest pass space is limited. Keep the throw explosive and clean.

exercises.name: 2. Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up progressively, then work up to one hard set with solid form. Stop if technique breaks. This session sets your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your training max.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if it feels more stable on the shoulders and upper back.

substitutionOptions.name: Goblet Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if barbell squatting is not yet safe or consistent. Work to a hard clean set in the same rep range.

exercises.name: 3. Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: Use a controlled lower and a strong press. Leave 2 reps in reserve on each set.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Bench Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you are comfortable with the setup and spotter access is good.

substitutionOptions.name: Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you need a simpler option. Elevate hands if needed to keep reps clean.

exercises.name: 4. Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Pull elbows back without shrugging. Leave 1-2 reps in reserve and keep the chest glued to the pad.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the chest-supported bench is taken. Keep the torso quiet.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a simple machine-based pull with steady tension.

exercises.name: 5. Ab Wheel Rollout

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Rollout
